qualitative.3m: Global athletic brand heritage and multi-decade sports sponsorship scale. Gross margins consistently remain around ~50% across cycles, though operating profitability fluctuates with footwear fashion trends and inventory clearing.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 15Y (global Three-Stripes athletic brand heritage & sports federation sponsorships 3_ia=1) reduced by -10Y across four moderate secular forces: falling DTC/OEM barriers enabling agile footwear entrants like On and Hoka (4_ent=1), intense global sponsorship & promotional rivalry with Nike, New Balance, Asics, and Puma (4_riv=1), Asian contract-factory tariff exposure & escalating club/athlete endorsement costs (4_sup=1), and fast 3-5 year lifestyle sneaker silhouette fatigue cycles (4_sub=1) -> Final CAP 5Y.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Athletic footwear and apparel face severe fashion-trend cycle risks, hit-franchise saturation (Samba/Gazelle fatigue), and intense market share erosion from agile challenger brands (On, Hoka). High Asian contract manufacturing exposure introduces persistent supply chain and tariff vulnerabilities. [Diagnostic G5=1 | G6=N: Standard stewardship under CEO Bjørn Gulden (prudent post-Yeezy dividend cut to €125M, buyback pause, minimal M&A and SBC; tempered by FY22 €2.53B peak-cycle buybacks), but fails Gate 6 on weak 5Y Owner FCF conversion (63.7%, with negative Owner FCF in FY22 -€1.86B and FY25 -€328M from working-capital swings) and failure to surpass its FY21 €10.89 Owner EPS peak despite 6.8x EBIT interest coverage.]
qualitative.evidence: Adidas generates over €21B in revenue across footwear (~50%+), apparel, and accessories. While gross margins have recovered to ~51% under CEO Bjørn Gulden following the termination of the Yeezy partnership, historical GAAP ROIC has been volatile (17.6% in 2019, 4.0% in 2022, -2.1% in 2023, recovering to ~8.5% in 2024). The business model is repeatedly subject to hit-franchise overproduction cycles (Stan Smith, Superstar, Boost, Yeezy, Samba) followed by promotional discounting. Supply chain is heavily dependent on outsourced factories in Vietnam, Indonesia, and China.

qualitative.3m: High-end brand prestige, alpine heritage, and controlled direct-to-consumer store network (~80%+ DTC) protect >29% operating margins and ROIC >20%. Strong pricing power in technical down jackets. Primary erosion threats include fashion fatigue, warming winter climates, narrow category concentration, and heavy dependence on Chinese consumer spending.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 15Y (contemporary alpine luxury outerwear brand prestige & controlled >80% DTC boutique network 3_ia=1, lacking multi-category century-old Lindy breadth) reduced by -5Y for Rivalry (4_riv=1: luxury houses Loro Piana, Prada, and Brunello Cucinelli expanding into luxury outerwear/skiwear) and Substitution (4_sub=1: single-category quilted down-jacket fashion fatigue and secularly warming winter climates) -> Final CAP 10Y.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Premium luxury outerwear brand with outstanding margins (~29% EBIT) and pristine net cash (>€1.4B), but structurally constrained by single-category seasonal product concentration (down jackets). Lacks the multi-category Lindy durability of century-old luxury houses and faces long-term headwinds from fashion cycle shifts and warming winter climates. [Diagnostic G5=2 | G6=Y: Elite owner-operator stewardship under Chairman/CEO Remo Ruffini (~16%+ stake), sustaining 76-78% gross and 29% EBIT margins via >80% controlled DTC full-price discipline, zero M&A bloat (0% ma_reinvest), and modest SBC (5.3% of NI); passes all Gate 6 pillars with 97.0% 5Y Owner FCF conversion, 10.7% peak-to-peak Owner EPS CAGR, €1.21B net cash (-1.81y), and 26.9x EBIT interest coverage.]
qualitative.evidence: FY2025 revenue of €3,132M and EBIT of €913M (29.2% margin) with net cash of €1.46B. Despite exceptional current profitability and >20% ROIC, Moncler brand generates >85% of group revenue, heavily skewed toward winter outerwear and Chinese luxury consumers (~50% Asia revenue). Narrow product category and fashion-trend sensitivity restrict 15+ year competitive advantage runway.

qualitative.3m: Iconic global intangible equity (Swoosh, Jordan Brand), Air/ZoomX footwear IP, unmatched pro-league and athlete endorsement scale ($46.4B revenue), and demand-creation budget prevent direct arbitrage by generic makers. Empirical proof across the cycle holds via 21.5% 10Y median ROIC (moderating to ~15% in FY25 and ~11.8%-18.7% in FY26 trough) and ~42.7%-42.9% trough gross margins, with selective FY26 tariff-offset price increases lifting gross margin +20 bps. Primary erosion threats are severe: global footwear share contracted from high-20s% toward low-20s% as On (>60% GM), Hoka, and Adidas captured running and lifestyle demand, while retro franchise over-supply and wholesale reset depressed FY25-FY26 net income ~45% below prior peaks.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 20Y (global Swoosh & Jordan brand intangibles and pro-league endorsements 3_ia=2, zero consumer switching costs 3_tb=0) reduced by -10Y for asset-light Asian contract factory access lowering insurgent entry barriers (4_ent=1), intense footwear share loss to On, Hoka, Adidas, and Anta/Li-Ning (4_riv=1), 95% Vietnam/Indonesia/China manufacturing & tariff concentration (4_sup=1), and 3-7Y footwear fashion/running innovation resets (4_sub=1) -> Final CAP 10Y.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). While Nike passes Gates 1-3 on transparent asset-light economics, entrenched everyday footwear/sportswear habits in Western markets, and multi-cycle intangible brand ROIC (21.5% historical median), its 20Y Initial CAP suffers a -10Y haircut to 10Y across competitive forces and macrotrends. Branded athletic footwear has zero switching costs, 3-7 year style/running-innovation cycles, and shared Asian contract factories, allowing agile insurgents (On, Hoka) and resurgent peers (Adidas, Anta/Li-Ning) to erode share rapidly—stalling FY26 revenue at $46.40B (+0.2%) and shrinking Net Income to $3.11B (-3.4%). Furthermore, 95% of NIKE Brand footwear is manufactured in Vietnam (52%), Indonesia (27%), and China (16%), leaving margins directly exposed to U.S. tariffs and geopolitical friction alongside persistent Greater China weakness. [Diagnostic G5=1 | G6=Y: Veteran CEO Elliott Hill halted share buybacks ($146M in FY25) to reset wholesale partnerships and clean accounting (0.4% ma_reinvest) following prior DTC/buyback missteps under Donahoe; passes Gate 6 on fortress balance sheet ($9.03B cash vs $7.94B funded debt ex-leases, -0.36y LT net debt, 24.2x interest coverage, $14.37B tangible equity), intact peak-to-peak history (p2p_ok=Y), and 85.8% 10Y Owner FCF conversion (92.3% 5Y GAAP FCF/NI despite a 77.2% 5Y Owner FCF trough dip).]
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financial record: Historical 10Y median ROIC is 21.5%. In FY25 (ended May 31, 2025), revenue dropped ~10% YoY (-9% currency-neutral) to $46,309M, gross profit fell 14% to $19,790M (~42.7% GM), Net Income fell ~44% to $3,219M, OCF was $3,698M (~$2.4B FCF), and ROIC moderated to ~15%. In FY26 (ended May 31, 2026), turnaround stabilization remained elusive: revenue was flat at $46,398M (+0.2% YoY), Net Income declined another ~3.4% to $3,108M, FCF slipped to ~$2.1B-$2.2B, and ROIC ranged ~11.8%-18.7% depending on capital adjustments, though gross margin edged up +20 bps to ~42.9% via selective pricing and inventory cleanup. Channel & regional mix: NIKE Direct fell from $18.8B (FY25) to $17.7B (FY26) as CEO Elliott Hill's 'Win Now' and 'Pace' plans re-engaged wholesale partners (Foot Locker, Dick's, JD Sports, specialty running), lifting North America wholesale at the cost of structurally lower wholesale unit gross margins while Greater China and EMEA remained soft. Supply chain & geopolitical concentration (FY25/FY26 10-Ks): 100% independent contract manufacturing; NIKE Brand footwear concentrated ~52% in Vietnam (51% FY25), ~27% in Indonesia (28% FY25), and ~16% in China (17% FY25), with 4 vendors representing ~59%-60% of footwear volume; apparel spanned 34 countries across 321 factories (303 in FY25). Balance sheet remained healthy at FY26 end ($9,030M cash & short-term investments vs $7,941M total debt), but structural fashion-cycle fade, specialty running share loss to On/Hoka, and unhedged Asian tariff/supply-chain exposure cap CAP at 10 years.

qualitative.3m: (1) Two-sided marketplace liquidity across 136M organic (147M total including Depop/Tise) active buyers, non-standard recommerce/collectibles/auto-parts inventory, and Authenticity Guarantee trust infrastructure prevents easy replication by generic retailers. (2) Empirically proven by ~18.2% historical median ROIC (2023: ~15.6-23.7%, 2024: ~14.8-21.7%, 2025: ~15.7-16.9%), 20.5% GAAP / 27.8% non-GAAP FY25 operating margins, and an ~13.9% ad-valorem GMV take rate (bolstered by $575M Q3 2026 Promoted Listings advertising) that scales with nominal price inflation. (3) Primary erosion threats are low seller/buyer switching costs and multi-homing against zero-fee C2C venues (Facebook Marketplace, Vinted), Amazon, Temu/Shein, and vertical specialists (Whatnot, StockX, Chrono24), capping base transaction fee expansion.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 20Y (two-sided recommerce/collectibles marketplace liquidity 3_tb=1 + global brand & Authenticity Guarantee network 3_ia=1) reduced by -10Y for vertical live-shopping/recommerce entrants (4_ent=1), multi-front rivalry from Amazon, Vinted, Facebook Marketplace, Whatnot & Temu (4_riv=1), frictionless multi-homing forcing European C2C seller-fee waivers (4_buy=1), and third-party AI shopping agents threatening Promoted Listings search monetization (4_sub=1) -> Final CAP 10Y.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Although eBay maintains a profitable two-sided recommerce and focus-category marketplace (72% of non-Depop GMV in Q3 2026) with ~25% 5Y GAAP ROIC, its 20Y Initial CAP receives a -10Y haircut to 10Y across four moderate competitive pressures. Core organic active buyers stagnated near 134-136M amid low switching costs and multi-homing, forcing defensive vertical M&A (Goldin, Tise, and the $1.2B Depop deal) and C2C fee concessions against Vinted/Facebook Marketplace, while third-party agentic AI shopping discovery threatens eBay's high-margin Promoted Listings sponsored-search monetization. [Diagnostic G5=1 | G6=N: Portfolio streamlining (PayPal/StubHub/Classifieds exits) and steady share count reduction (1,119M to 460M) support standard Gate 5 stewardship despite heavy SBC ($607M = 30% of FY25 NI, 730 bps GAAP/non-GAAP spread) and $1.2B defensive Depop M&A; fails Gate 6 on absent peak-to-peak compounding (p2p_ok=N, decade-flat ~$2.3B EBIT, declining Owner FCF from $2.07B in FY19 to $1.17B in FY25) and sub-80% FCF conversion (37.5% reported 5Y; ~58-61% ex-non-cash equity marks) alongside tangible equity thinned to $148M by buybacks exceeding FCF.]
qualitative.evidence: FY 2025 revenue reached $11.1B (+8% YoY as-reported, +7% FXN) on $79.6B GMV (+7% YoY, +6% FXN), with >40% of GMV in recommerce, 20.5% GAAP operating margin (27.8% non-GAAP, 730 bps SBC/adjustment spread), $2.03B GAAP net income, and ~$1.43-1.50B FCF (~70-74% GAAP NI conversion in FY25 vs ~99% in FY24 on $1.96B FCF / $1.98B NI and ~71% in FY23 on $1.97B FCF / $2.77B NI). Momentum accelerated in 2026 (Q1 rev $3.09B, Q2 rev $3.13B / GMV $22.4B, Q3 rev $3.21B +14% YoY / GMV $23.2B +15% YoY) aided by Focus Categories/recommerce/C2C (>20% YoY growth), Promoted Listings ($575M in Q3 2026), eBay Live, and the $1.2B acquisition of Depop plus Tise, which lifted total active buyers from ~134-136M organic to 147M. Historical ROIC stands at ~18.2% median (~15.7-16.9% in 2025). Year-end 2025 cash and fixed-income investments of $4.8B (plus >$900M equity stakes) against $6.7B gross debt (~$1.9B net debt) keep leverage modest alongside ~$2B/yr share buyback targets, following earlier divestitures of PayPal, StubHub, and Classifieds.

qualitative.3m: Proprietary low-power GPS hardware, Firstbeat physiological algorithms, FAA/EASA-certified cockpit avionics, and vertical manufacturing create high technical barriers and Garmin Connect/avionics ecosystem switching costs. Empirically proved by 23.94% 5Y median GAAP ROIC (26.88% tangible ROIC), ~25.5% 5Y incremental ROIIC on net operating capital, 58.7% FY2025 gross margin, and 25.9% EBIT margin despite flagship ASP tiering and tariff pressures. Primary erosion threats are Apple/Samsung/Coros smartwatch encroachment in consumer wearables and Taiwan manufacturing concentration.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 20Y (low-power GNSS/sensor/avionics R&D 3_rd=1 + FAA-certified cockpit & Garmin Connect switching friction 3_tb=1 + specialist brand/certifications 3_ia=1) reduced by -10Y for Apple/Samsung/Coros smartwatch & Auto OEM rivalry across ~71% of revenue (4_riv=1), single-country Taiwan manufacturing concentration & tariff exposure (4_sup=1), and fast consumer-electronics hardware clock speed (4_sub=1) -> Final CAP 10Y.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). While Garmin is a debt-free, high-ROIC (~24.9% 5Y GAAP ROIC) engineering franchise across GPS wearables, certified avionics, and marine electronics, its 20Y Initial CAP receives a -10Y competitive-force haircut to 10Y. Roughly 61.5% Fitness/Outdoor consumer wearables and 9.2% Auto OEM exposure carry fast consumer-electronics clock speed (4_sub=1) and intense Apple/Samsung/Coros rivalry (4_riv=1), compounded by severe single-country manufacturing concentration in Taiwan (Tainan/northern Taiwan plants) exposed to cross-strait geopolitical risk and U.S. tariffs (4_sup=1)—failing the Munger 15+ year Secular Resilience bar. [Diagnostic G5=2 | G6=Y: Co-founder Dr. Min Kao and 37-year insider CEO Cliff Pemble exemplify owner-operator organic compounding—growing Owner EPS 3.2x over 10 years ($2.70 to $8.59) at 24.9% ROIC with minimal M&A ($760M goodwill on $8.97B equity), low SBC (10% of NI), and zero funded debt; passes Gate 6 with record peak-to-peak Owner EPS (10.7% CAGR), $2.74B cash vs zero LT funded debt (-1.53y net debt, 99x interest coverage, $8.01B tangible equity), and 80.2% 10Y Owner FCF conversion (99.7% 2Y OCF/NI; 74.8% 5Y reflects FY21-22 inventory/capex build).]
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financial record (FY2016-FY2025, SEC EDGAR): Sales grew from $3,018.7M to $7,245.5M (+15% YoY in FY2025), EBIT expanded from $632.9M (21.0% margin) to $1,876.1M (25.9% margin), Net Income rose from $517.7M to $1,663.9M, and Owner EPS compounded from $2.73 to $8.59 (10.7% 5Y CAGR), with only a -2.5% sales dip in FY2022. Capital efficiency stayed consistently above hurdle: GAAP ROIC ranged 16.85%-27.12% (5Y median 23.94%), tangible ROIC 19.03%-30.62% (5Y median 26.88%), and 5Y incremental ROIIC (FY2020-FY2025 delta NI / delta equity ex-cash) was ~25.5%. FY2025 gross margin held at 58.7% despite tariffs; 5Y Owner FCF conversion was 75.72% ($4,861.6M / $6,420.7M, dragged by 2021-2022 inventory/capex build and $166.0M FY2025 SBC; 10Y Owner FCF conversion 80.17%). Balance sheet holds $0.0M LT debt and $2,278.6M cash. FY2025 segment revenue: Fitness $2.36B (~32.5%), Outdoor $2.10B (~29%), Marine $1.20B (~16.5%), Aviation $987M (~13.6%), Auto OEM $665M (~9.2%). Governance & M&A: Co-founder Executive Chairman Dr. Min Kao (~0.86%-1% stake) and CEO Cliff Pemble (1989 employee #6, CEO since 2013) favor organic R&D and disciplined bolt-ons (goodwill/intangibles $760.2M vs $8,972.6M equity) plus $663.9M dividends. Gate 4 failure driver: FY2025 Form 10-K confirms principal consumer manufacturing facilities (including fēnix/Enduro lines in Tainan Tree Valley) are concentrated in Taiwan, creating direct Macrotrend [3] vulnerability to cross-strait conflict, regional airspace/shipping disruption, and high tariff regimes, compounded by ongoing consumer smartwatch platform competition.

qualitative.3m: Brand equity and proprietary footwear design IP across UGG ($2.74B FY26 sales) and HOKA ($2.59B FY26 sales), reinforced by strict wholesale allocation and full-price selling discipline. Empirically verified by 28.5% historical median ROIC (30-35%+ in FY25-FY26), 57.9% FY25 gross margin, and 23.1%-23.7% operating margins even amid promotional industry discounting. Primary erosion threats: zero customer switching costs, fashion/silhouette cyclicality, and surging running rivals (On Holding, Salomon, Nike, Adidas).
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 15Y (UGG & HOKA footwear brand equity and full-price wholesale allocation 3_ia=1, zero switching costs 3_tb=0) reduced by -10Y for low contract-factory entry barriers for insurgent running labels (4_ent=1), fierce rivalry from On, Salomon, Nike & Adidas (4_riv=1), outsourced Vietnam/Asian manufacturing tariff exposure (4_sup=1), and footwear fashion/silhouette cyclicality (4_sub=1) -> Final CAP 5Y.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While UGG and HOKA generate elite current ROIC and ~23% operating margins via brand intangibles and full-price discipline, a two-brand footwear house with zero customer switching costs starts at a 15Y Initial CAP and suffers a -10Y competitive-force haircut to 5Y. Shared Asian contract factories enable rapid insurgent entry, HOKA faces decelerating growth against On Holding, Salomon, Nike, and Adidas alongside UGG fashion-cycle rotation, and outsourced Vietnam/SE Asian shoe assembly leaves margins directly exposed to ~20%+ U.S. tariffs without viable domestic reshoring. [Diagnostic G5=1 | G6=Y: Disciplined full-price channel management (57.7% gross margin, 23.1% EBIT margin), tiny SBC (4.4% of FY25 NI), zero M&A dilution ($14M goodwill), and cash-funded share retirement (193.9M to 147.2M shares since FY16) earn a strong Gate 5 pass under new 2024 leadership; passes all Gate 6 pillars cleanly with 94.2% 5Y Owner FCF conversion, 24.9% peak-to-peak Owner EPS CAGR, $1.91B cash vs zero funded debt (-1.63y net debt, 362x interest coverage), and $2.47B tangible equity.]
qualitative.evidence: FY25 net sales rose 16.3% to $4.986B (UGG $2.531B +13.1%, HOKA $2.233B +23.6%, Other $221.2M -8.6%) with gross margin expanding to 57.9% (from 55.6% in FY24) and operating income of $1.183B (~23.7% margin). FY26 net sales rose 9.8% to $5.472B (UGG $2.74B +8.2%, HOKA $2.59B +15.9%, non-core labels streamlined including Sanuk divestiture/exit) with operating income of $1.263B (~23.1% margin) and FCF above $1.1B. Historical median ROIC is 28.5% (30-35%+ recently). Management (CEO Stefano Caroti, CFO Steve Fasching) enforces full-price selling to protect brand equity despite U.S. DTC volume friction, operates essentially debt-free with $1.6B-$1.9B cash, repurchased 10.5M shares for $1.075B in FY26, and raised buyback authorization by $3.5B in May 2026 (~$5B total). Fails 15Y Munger runway bar due to zero switching costs, HOKA growth normalization amidst fierce competition, and Vietnam/SE Asia tariff concentration.

qualitative.3m: Scale economies shared via massive direct procurement of fresh, responsibly sourced ingredients and industry-leading restaurant throughput ($3.2M+ AUV across 4,000+ company-owned locations). Insurmountable unit cost advantages allow CMG to deliver high-protein, 1.5-lb+ entrees at accessible price points that fragmented fast-casual peers cannot replicate at scale. Moat proved by multi-year GAAP ROIC consistently exceeding 20% (and operating ROIC >45%) alongside successful cumulative price realization passing through ingredient and wage inflation. Primary erosion threats: brand fatigue / portion perception backlash, unit-level labor cost escalation, and aggressive copycat fast-casual concepts.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 20Y (fast-casual brand/Chipotlane footprint 3_ia=1 + high-throughput $3.2M AUV procurement/value efficiency 3_se=1, zero switching costs 3_tb=0) reduced by -10Y for low fast-casual entry barriers (4_ent=1), aggressive QSR/fast-casual value rivalry (4_riv=1), and unbuffered hourly kitchen labor & fresh-ingredient inflation across 4,000+ 100%-company-owned restaurants (4_sup=1) -> Final CAP 10Y.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). While Chipotle has built a strong fast-casual brand with $3.2M+ unit volumes and debt-free capital efficiency, its 20Y Initial CAP receives a -10Y haircut to 10Y across low restaurant entry barriers (Cava, Sweetgreen, copycat bowl chains), QSR value wars, and unbuffered labor/ingredient inflation. Operating 4,042 100%-company-owned restaurants employing ~120,000 hourly workers without a franchise royalty buffer leaves margins directly exposed to demographic labor scarcity and statutory minimum-wage hikes (compressing restaurant-level margins from 27.4% to 23.3% in 2026 alongside portion/pricing pushback), failing the 15-year Munger longevity bar. [Diagnostic G5=1 | G6=Y: High-ROI store expansion ($3.2M+ AUV, <2Y cash payback), zero M&A bloat ($21.9M goodwill), modest SBC (7.8% of NI), and cash-funded buybacks support standard Gate 5 stewardship following the 2024 CEO transition to Scott Boatwright amid portion-size pushback; passes all Gate 6 pillars with 109.4% 5Y Owner FCF conversion, 36.1% peak-to-peak Owner EPS CAGR, zero long-term funded debt ($1.04B cash, -0.75y net debt, 99x interest coverage), and $2.81B tangible equity.]
qualitative.evidence: Chipotle grew revenue from $6.0B in 2020 to $11.3B in 2024 and $11.9B in 2025, with operating income of $1.94B (16.2% operating margin). High capital efficiency is demonstrated by multi-year GAAP ROIC of 20-47%, supported by $3.2M+ average unit volumes (AUV) and sub-2-year cash payback on new builds across 4,042 restaurants. Pristine balance sheet with zero funded debt (only operating lease liabilities of $5.1B) and ~$1B+ in cash and short-term investments. FCF conversion tracks 80-85% of net income ($1.15B FCF on $1.4B net income). However, the 100% company-operated store model leaves Chipotle directly exposed to accelerating hourly labor inflation (e.g. California AB 1228 $20/hr minimum wage), requiring continuous labor investments that compressed restaurant-level margins from 27.4% to 23.3% in 2026. Executive leadership transition to CEO Scott Boatwright in late 2024 has necessitated deliberate margin concessions to protect transaction traffic and resolve consumer portion-size pushback, underscoring secular labor and consumer sensitivity limits.

qualitative.3m: Global store density, proprietary ethical coffee sourcing/roasting infrastructure, and the Starbucks Rewards digital ecosystem (~34M+ active US members with substantial prepaid stored-value float) create high customer repeat frequency and scale advantages over independent cafes. Empirical proof includes a 10-year median ROIC of 22.8% and gross margins near 68-70%. Primary erosion threats include value-conscious customer pushback on premium pricing, beverage preparation complexity eroding throughput, rapid low-cost automated rivals in international markets (e.g. Luckin in China), and store-level labor friction.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 20Y (global coffeehouse brand & dense store/roasting footprint 3_ia=2, zero contractual switching costs 3_tb=0) reduced by -10Y for low drive-thru kiosk/pick-up coffee entry barriers (4_ent=1), fierce Luckin/Dutch Bros/QSR beverage rivalry that forced a 2026 China JV retreat (4_riv=1), ~400k barista labor/union friction & Arabica bean volatility (4_sup=1), and at-home espresso/RTD energy substitution (4_sub=1) -> Final CAP 10Y.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). While Starbucks commands an iconic global coffee brand and habitual daily ritual, its 20Y Initial CAP suffers a -10Y haircut to 10Y under secular macrotrends and competitive forces. Demographic labor scarcity and unionization create persistent bottlenecks and wage inflation across ~400,000 store workers where complex handcrafted drinks resist automation, while low-cost automated rivals (Luckin Coffee in China, forcing a 2026 licensed-JV retreat, and rapid US drive-thru chains like Dutch Bros/7 Brew) eroded traffic and compressed FY25 EBIT margins to 7.9%. [Diagnostic G5=1 | G6=N: Turnaround CEO Brian Niccol halted share buybacks ($0 in FY25-26) and refocused on core store throughput with clean accounting and modest SBC following prior China/operational missteps; however, fails Gate 6 on the automatic debt-funded buyback red flag—prior $17.4B (FY18-19) and $6.3B (FY22-24) leveraged buybacks created a -$7.67B stockholders' deficit (-$9.09B tangible equity) and $22.4B total debt ($18.7B net debt including store leases, ~7.4x FY26 NI) with $2.82B dividends exceeding net income.]
qualitative.evidence: FY2025 revenue was $37.2B with operating income compressing to $2.9B (7.9% operating margin) before recovering toward $2.5B+ net income in FY2026 under Brian Niccol's 'Back to Starbucks' turnaround. 10-year median ROIC is 22.8%, proving historical brand power and returns on capital. However, traffic declines in 2024-2025 demonstrated pricing elasticity limits for $7+ handcrafted drinks. In China, relentless low-cost competition from Luckin Coffee forced a structural conversion of retail operations into a licensed JV in 2026. The balance sheet carries ~$14.6B-$15.0B in long-term debt against net income of $1.86B-$2.53B (debt/net income ~5.8x-7.8x) and a total stockholders' deficit of $(8.1B) resulting from aggressive debt-funded share repurchases.

qualitative.3m: MAX in-app bidding mediation commands ~70-80% share in mobile gaming, imposing high SDK migration friction and A/B revenue-loss risk on publishers, while coupling MAX auction clearing-price visibility with the AXON ML recommendation engine creates a potent two-sided data network effect. Empirical proof: 5Y median GAAP ROIC exceeds 12% (~14-18%; financials baseline 18.5%), surging from ~3.3% (FY21) and -0.8% (FY22) to ~12.5-14.9% (FY23), ~31-42% (FY24), and ~82-95% (FY25) with >100% tangible operating ROIC and operating margins expanding to 75.8% (FY25) and ~76-78% (2026). Performance auctions capture nominal ad-spend inflation ad valorem. Primary erosion threats: unilateral Apple iOS / Google Android OS privacy and attribution policy changes, EU GDPR litigation, and rival ML ad-bidding convergence from vertically integrated walled gardens (Meta, Alphabet, Amazon) and Unity LevelPlay.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 20Y (MAX SDK mediation switching friction 3_tb=1 + AXON ML bidding R&D 3_rd=1) capped via Fatal-Flaw rule for severe Apple iOS / Google Android walled-garden OS attribution & privacy dependency (4_sup=2, as seen in the FY22 ATT margin collapse), alongside ML bidding rivalry from vertically integrated ad hegemons (4_riv=1) and fast ad-tech/AI clock speed (4_sub=1) -> Final CAP 5Y.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While AppLovin possesses a potent near-term mediation switching-cost and ML auction flywheel (MAX + AXON) with extraordinary 2024-2026 economics, it fails the 15-year Mauboussin predictability and Munger disruption bar. Starting from a 20Y Initial CAP, Fatal-Flaw supplier/platform risk (4_sup=2) plus ad-tech rivalry and fast AI clock speed cap Final CAP at 5Y: unlike vertically integrated AI hegemons owning consumer surfaces and OS infrastructure (Alphabet, Meta, Apple), AppLovin owns neither the mobile OS, app store, nor first-party consumer apps (having divested its Apps unit in June 2025).
